transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-01 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET
- Duration: ~56 minutes
- Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Maria Espinoza (Cordova Head of ML Ops), Samir Khan (Platform Eng), Dana Lee (SRE), Oliver Price (Product)

Summary:
Quick Q2 operational sync to review usage trends, cost pressure from holiday catalog launches, latency regressions seen last week, and alignment on a Reserved Capacity pilot. Goal is to decide pilot scope and next steps for capacity commit/benchmarking.

[00:00] Liam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about an hour. we'll run through a quick health snapshot, a couple of things we flagged on p95, and then the reserved capacity options. Maria, Samir, Dana, you all still good with this agenda?

[00:18] Maria Espinoza: Yep, sounds good. brief context: last weekend we saw a traffic uptick from the regional promo and p95 spiked from 320ms to 1.2s on the inference layer, and that pushed internal timeouts. we did some quick retries but want more durable plan.

[00:34] Priya Nair: Got it, thanks. quick note: the spike looked like prefix cache misses + burst batching behavior — sequence lengths were longer for the product descriptions, which amplified KV cache pressure.

[00:55] Samir Khan: there was also an increase in concurrent sessions from the mobile app, so QPS went up around 2.6x for a 25 minute window. our autoscale kicked in but we hit a cold-start tail and throttled.

[01:12] Liam Carter: Perfect. I'll pull up the perf summary deck we dropped in the invite. (link: /decks/cordova-q2-health.pdf) Priya, can you share what the profile means from a runtime perspective?

[01:28] Priya Nair: Sure. high-level: when sequence length distribution shifts right it increases per-token compute and kernel saturation. our runtime detects this and will favor lower-latency kernels but cost per token jumps. also, if KV cache reuse drops—because many requests start new prefixes—you lose the typical 30-45% token savings. That maps to both higher latency and higher spend.

[01:52] Dana Lee: is that the same as the "prefix cache" you mentioned previously? we've been seeing a lot more unique session IDs from mobile.

[02:06] Priya Nair: yes, exactly. unique prefixes + longer sequences = worse batching efficiency. One mitigation is to increase conservative batching windows, but that adds latency tail risk. tradeoff.

[02:24] Oliver Price: What I want to understand is: for the peak campaign week, what is the delta in cost if we move to Reserved vs keeping on Hosted burst? we need a predictability number for finance.

[02:39] Liam Carter: Good question. we prepared two scenarios — a reserved capacity flat commit that covers baseline QPS + 20% headroom, and a hybrid burst plan where you keep hosted for spiky delta. We'll share the spreadsheet, but back-of-envelope: reserved commit reduces unit cost by roughly 27-33% on your high-memory model family given your mix. I'll send the numbers after this call.

[03:05] Maria Espinoza: Are those numbers accounting for quantized variants? we use a quantized 8-bit model in staging but prod still runs bfloat.

[03:19] Priya Nair: We modeled a few quantization profiles. Typically a 4-bit/8-bit LLM variant can cut per-token GPU time by 20-35% depending on accuracy tolerance. For Cordova's NLG product descriptions, we ran evals last month showing negligible quality drop for 8-bit; 4-bit had some token-deletions on rare templated prompts.

[03:45] Samir Khan: okay. security question: if we commit reserved capacity, can we still run that in our VPC for data residency? we can't send certain PII out.

[03:57] Liam Carter: Yes — Redwood Dedicated can be private VPC peering or a private deployment (Private). For Dedicated reserved pools we offer customer VPC peering and KMS integration. we'll share the network checklist.

[04:14] Dana Lee: Do you have SOC2 + ISO artifacts? our security team will require them for the PO.

[04:23] Janelle Ortiz: Absolutely. I'll upload SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 summary, and the standard hardening checklist to the slack channel by EOD. I'll also include an excerpt of our audit log schema.

[04:38] Maria Espinoza: Great, thanks. back to latency: Priya, could you walk through the tail analysis you ran on the 05/28 incident?

[04:51] Priya Nair: yeah. we correlated GPU utilization to p95 across the affected region. What we saw: a small set of requests with long sequences induced KV eviction and caused subsequent requests to miss the cache for the same worker — that caused a cascade of higher per-token time for a few minutes. There was also an interplay with our batching window; when the window tried to gather more samples under higher QPS, it sometimes extended the token latency for the first packet.

[05:24] Samir Khan: Is there a safe tweak to reduce the p95 without a big cost hit? perhaps tune the batching policy or lower max sequence cap for certain routes?

[05:37] Priya Nair: A couple options: 1) conservative per-route throttling to keep critical real-time endpoints under a lower batching window; 2) enable per-route KV prewarm for expected prefixes; 3) allocate a small dedicated pool (Reserved) for the real-time path while routing non-critical responses to a higher-batch pool. Option 3 is slightly more expensive overall but isolates the real-time p95.

[06:04] Maria Espinoza: Option 3 sounds promising — we can't have product description generation slow for checkout flows. What's the estimated extra cost?

[06:16] Liam Carter: For the isolation pool sized to your checkout QPS, the incremental cost is modest compared to what p95 outages cost you in conversion. We'll attach a scenario sheet; it's about a 7-12% uplift on total monthly spend in the worst case but drops p95 by ~40% for the isolated route.

[06:41] Oliver Price: Can we do an A/B on routing to prove it? maybe small canary for two region clusters?

[06:49] Priya Nair: Yes — we can do a canary / gradual rollout with automatic fallback policies built into rollouts. Redwood Console supports per-route model pinning and fallback to hosted variants. We'll help set a rollout policy.

[07:04] Dana Lee: On networking, we need to make sure the Dedicated pool's egress IPs match our firewall allow list. Samir will share the list.

[07:14] Samir Khan: Yep, I'll export that. Also one more thing — we've seen an odd error pattern in the logs: a small percentage of requests return partial output with no error code. Any idea?

[07:26] Priya Nair: That often shows up when there's a KV cache eviction mid-stream or a worker preemption that interrupts the stream. We'll need the raw trace IDs to debug. Maria, if you can send 3 sample trace IDs we can look in the backend logs.

[07:44] Maria Espinoza: I'll pull those and upload them.

[07:50] Liam Carter: Good. let's pivot to pilot scope: we're recommending a two-week reserved pilot that simulates your holiday catalog week plus two isolated day-long spike tests. During pilot we'll run the same prompts and traffic replay we use in your staging harness. Priya will coordinate the harness.

[08:10] Priya Nair: For the pilot we need: (1) traffic replay file + sequence length histogram, (2) a set of eval prompts for quality check, (3) target SLOs — p50/p95 token latency and error budget. We'll provide the runner and the metrics dashboard.

[08:28] Oliver Price: On SLOs — our target is p95 < 350ms for checkout-critical routes, and p95 < 700ms for bulk description generation. Is that achievable?

[08:39] Priya Nair: For the checkout route yes, with either dedicated pool or lower batching window. For bulk generation, hybrid approach with cached prefixes will likely meet 700ms. We'll validate in the pilot.

[08:52] Samir Khan: One blockers question: what's the lead time for reserved pool capacity if we sign a monthly commit?

[09:03] Liam Carter: For Dedicated reserved pools in cloud regions we can provision within 5-7 business days for modest sizes; for larger multi-GPU footprints it can take 10-14 days. If you need on-prem private deployment lead times are longer.

[09:19] Maria Espinoza: Okay good. finance will want a hard number before the campaign kickoff. can you give a best-effort estimate today?

[09:27] Liam Carter: We'll send the committed vs hybrid scenario spreadsheet after the call — two options: conservative commit (baseline+20%) and aggressive commit (baseline+50% with discount). I'll flag the expected monthly spend and effective unit cost.

[09:41] Dana Lee: Quick security nuance — if we use KMS, are keys in our tenant or managed by Redwood?

[09:49] Priya Nair: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated. For Hosted variants we can do envelope encryption with customer KMS depending on contract. We'll include the KMS integration notes in the security packet.

[10:02] Maria Espinoza: Also curious about audit logs for model access. we need immutable logs for regulatory reasons.

[10:10] Janelle Ortiz: Our audit logging includes token-level request IDs, model version, and user identity where available — and we can push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder. I'll include the sample log format.

[10:23] Oliver Price: Competitors — we're also talking to Anthropic about a similar dedicated pricing — how is Redwood differentiating here on reliability?

[10:33] Liam Carter: Two diffs: 1) our serving runtime has built-in KV caching and per-route rollout controls which improve tail isolation; 2) we offer blended Reserved+burst patterns with transparent per-token analytics so you can measure cost vs latency tradeoffs. We'll share a short benchmark note comparing tail behavior in heavy-long-sequence workloads.

[10:55] Samir Khan: That benchmark will be useful. any chance to see a real trace of a long-seq request and how KV evictions look?

[11:05] Priya Nair: Yes — we'll export a sample trace and annotate the timeline. Maria, we'll coordinate to get the trace IDs.

[11:14] Maria Espinoza: I'll gather them.

[11:20] Liam Carter: Recap and next steps: 1) Redwood to deliver two pricing scenarios + blended cost sheet (Liam) 2) Redwood to provision pilot harness and run initial smoke test (Priya) 3) Cordova to share traffic profile, sample traces, and firewall CIDRs (Maria & Samir) 4) Redwood to upload security artifacts (Janelle). Any other asks?

[11:42] Dana Lee: Nothing else from infra.

[11:46] Oliver Price: Product will review the pilot eval prompts and confirm quality thresholds.

[11:50] Liam Carter: Great. we'll aim to have the pricing + pilot window scheduled by 2026-06-04, and initial pilot run by 2026-06-09.

[11:59] Maria Espinoza: Sounds good. thanks everyone.

[12:05] Liam Carter: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links.

End notes: Links shared during call: /decks/cordova-q2-health.pdf, /sheets/cordova-reserved-scenarios.xlsx, security packet link (uploaded to slack).
